transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya P., Jonas R., Lena O., Marcus C., Priya S.

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — can you hear me?
[00:00:05] Lena: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:00:07] Marcus: here.
[00:00:10] Priya: Hello.
[00:00:12] Maya: Great. So this is our renewal and capacity planning sync. We'll run through usage, the reserve packages, and then region options — Lena I know you flagged EU and APAC.
[00:00:27] Jonas: (screen share) I pulled the last 90 days of token throughput and concurrent slot usage, there are a couple spikes we should call out, looks like mid-June we saw sustained 40 concurrent with bursts to 75 for 10 minutes.
[00:00:42] Marcus: Yeah that was our end-of-quarter recruitment drive, lots of inference for resume parsing and chat assists.
[00:00:49] Maya: Right, and current committed reserved capacity is 50 concurrent. Your renewal is up in 6 weeks so we wanted to talk upgrade scenarios: a modest bump to 75, a more durable bump to 100, or an aggressive 150 plan with burst credits.
[00:01:05] Lena: From platform standpoint, 75 might be safe for normal ops but recruitment spikes are unpredictable, so 100 gives margin. For EU we need local residency for audit logs and some outputs — can't leave logs in US.
[00:01:19] Priya: On procurement, our standard is 12 months but we can consider 18 if there's a cost advantage, procurement window opens after next Tuesday.
[00:01:27] Jonas: Noted. On pricing, pro-rated add-on for the remainder of the current term is straightforward; for the upcoming term we can show 12-month and 18-month committed discount tiers.
[00:01:38] [00:01:40] Speaker 1: Uh, one question — if we move to 150 reserved does that require private deployment or can hosted handle it?
[00:01:46] Jonas: Good question. Hosted can absolutely handle 150 persistent slots; it'll just change the cost and the way we allocate on our Dedicated pool. Private (VPC/on-prem) is separate and we'd need a scoping session.
[00:01:58] Marcus: We also care about network egress and latency from EU — any chance we can have a controlled cutover window?
[00:02:05] Maya: Absolutely. For EU region we can schedule a canary cutover, and Redwood has routing policies so you can pin traffic regionally.
[00:02:12] Lena: On compliance: SOC2 in place, do you have ISO certs? Also we need to integrate with our SAML SSO and our KMS for key rotations.
[00:02:21] Jonas: We have SOC2 plus a pending ISO audit — we'll share the certs. SAML SSO is supported, and KMS integration (K M S) is available for private — for hosted we have customer-managed keys via a dedicated module, but I should double-check exact key rotation semantics — I'll include that in the benchmark doc.
[00:02:40] [00:02:45] Priya: Any risk of vendor lock if we go 18 months? Procurement asks about exit clauses and data export.
[00:02:52] Maya: Standard exit terms apply; we allow data export and a 90-day handover for customers moving off. We can also include a rollback policy if you want a staged exit.
[00:03:03] Jonas: For performance, I ran a quick synthetic: on gen-medium model with the current token shapes, 50->100 concurrent increases p95 latency from ~120ms to ~160ms under same batching config, but with better batching/timeouts we can keep p95 closer to 140ms. For 150 concurrent you do see more variance — there it's critical to use our KV caching and adaptive batching.
[00:03:27] Marcus: Can you share the exact test harness so we can run it in our staging? We want to validate with our real prompts.
[00:03:34] Jonas: Yep, I'll send the harness and also a spreadsheet of latency percentiles by concurrency and model.
[00:03:40] [00:03:45] Lena: Regarding EU cutover, our security team needs audit logs kept in EU datastores and access controls with RBAC — can Redwood write logs to our S3 in eu-west-1?
[00:03:55] Maya: We support log forwarding and can route audit streams to your S3 bucket in eu-west-1. There's a little setup on the console — we'll document steps.
[00:04:04] Priya: About billing: if we bump mid-term do we get pro-rated credits? Also what about burst credits — how do those show on invoice?
[00:04:12] Maya: Pro-rata yes, we'll issue an adjusted invoice for the remainder of the term. Burst credits show as a separate line item with usage details. We'll include sample invoice examples.
[00:04:21] [00:04:30] Marcus: SLA question — if we move to higher reserved tier does SLA improve? We need 99.9 for some HR-facing endpoints.
[00:04:37] Maya: SLA is tied to the Dedicated/Reserved tier. 99.9 is available at the 100+ reserved tier with extra monitoring and on-call support. We can also set up synthetic checks from your endpoints to validate availability.
[00:04:48] Jonas: Also worth noting fallback routing — if EU capacity is saturated we can fall back to a compatible model in another region with anonymization. That lowers latency guarantees but keeps availability.
[00:05:00] Lena: For APAC pilot, we only need a small footprint — 10 concurrent reserved for the first 3 months. Can that be attached to the main contract?
[00:05:07] Maya: Yes, multi-region attachments are supported — we'll show a blended price.
[00:05:11] Priya: On the legal side, any special clauses for data processed in APAC we should be aware of?
[00:05:15] Maya: No special clauses beyond standard data processing addendum; if you have country-specific needs call them out and we'll escalate to legal.
[00:05:23] [00:05:25] Speaker 2: I'm seeing a note about caching — how does KV cache behave across regions?
[00:05:29] Jonas: KV cache is per-region for latency reasons. For global consistency you can use an application-level sync or use our prefix caching config; it's not a global replicated cache by default.
[00:05:42] Marcus: Okay that helps. Also for some of our endpoints we use embeddings and reranking — does that affect slot sizing?
[00:05:48] Jonas: Embeddings are charged differently (per-embedding unit) but they do incur GPU memory and pipeline time; reranking can be batched separately. We'll include guidance in the sizing doc.
[00:05:58] [00:06:05] Lena: Can you talk through a suggested migration plan for EU? We want minimal customer impact.
[00:06:09] Jonas: Suggested: 1) Provision EU reserved 2) Set up canary routes at 5-10% traffic for 48hrs 3) Monitor latency/error/quality 4) Ramp to 50% then full cutover across a weekend, with rollback flagged. We'll provide a runbook and a playbook for rollbacks.
[00:06:25] Priya: That schedule works with our release windows if we target mid-August.
[00:06:29] Maya: Great. Quick commercial recap — we'll put three options in the quote: 12-month (baseline), 18-month (discounted), and an aggressive 150 concurrent with burst credits. We'll also include the APAC pilot as an attachment.
[00:06:45] Marcus: Are there any onboarding costs for the EU region?
[00:06:49] Maya: Minimal setup fee for region provisioning and audit log routing — I'll call it out in the quote.
[00:06:56] [00:07:00] Lena: One final: benchmarking — please include real prompt templates, not synthetic short ones; we want to see worst-case tails.
[00:07:07] Jonas: Will do. I'll include sample prompts and a long-tail run.
[00:07:12] Maya: Ok, let's summarize next steps. Jonas will run the throughput benchmark and share results; I'll send the updated pricing with pro-rata and 18-month options; Priya will provide procurement timing; Lena will confirm EU residency specifics. Anything else?
[00:07:27] Priya: I'll also request internal legal to look at the DPA and revert.
[00:07:30] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and post the deck and the benchmark sheet.
[00:07:36] [00:07:40] End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label swaps (Speaker 1/2 appear), minor OCR-like mis-words (K M S separated), and dropped punctuation typical of automated call transcriptions.
